ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: APAC inference cluster (apac1) reporting sustained 500s and token-latency spike >1200ms across public endpoints. Aggregated error-rate 6.4% over 5m window. Paging on-call.
Alex W: seeing this on dashboards too, spikes started ~5m ago after a deploy? 500s mostly model-inference-timeouts.
Mira Chen: I’m on-call, grabbing it. Can someone post the deploy id if any?
Juan P: no deploys flagged in last 30m from deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: no active deploys in apac1 for service redwood-runtime (last deploy 00:48 UTC).
Samir R: quick check of provider metrics — underlying GPU hosts in apac1 show intermittent NVLINK errors and pod restarts around same time. Likely degraded provider availability, causing queue/backpressure.
Mira Chen: ok, severity P1. Customer-facing error rate rising, paging escalation to SRE. Plan: start traffic steering to fallback provider pool in region (apac2) + soft brownout non-critical features.
Katie L: steps? I can flip gates and adjust quotas.
Mira Chen: 1) increase per-tenant rate limit to protect hosts? actually reduce non-SLA tenant qps by 30% to relieve pressure. 2) disable high-cost feature gate "tools.reranker" and fall back to basic ranking, 3) toggle routing to prefer provider apac2 for new sessions.
Alex W: recommend prefix-caching for large prompt prefixes while we steer. Also enable 503->429 transform on edge to surface quota to clients rather than backend timeouts.
Juan P: executing traffic-steer runbook now. Running routing command to shift 40% traffic to apac2 as canary: `./routingctl --region apac --from apac1 --to apac2 --pct 40 --sticky false`
Juan P: (output) OK: started asynchronous move job job_id=rb-2201-canary-42
Samir R: starting to see fall in queue depth on apac1 for canary sessions. Latency for canary path stable ~220ms.
Katie L: applying feature gate: `featurectl set tools.reranker=false --region apac --reason "brownout"`
Katie L: feature gate applied. Notifying growth teams.
Mira Chen: adjusting quota packs — backend config update `quotactl update --region apac --target non_sla --scale 0.7`
Mira Chen: quota change propagated. Expect minimal churn but should drop QPS from heavy tenants.
Alex W: posting customer-facing note draft: "We are experiencing elevated errors in APAC. We are steering traffic to alternate capacity and temporarily disabling advanced ranking to preserve availability. Some requests may see increased latency or reduced ranking fidelity. Working on full restoration." Should we send status page?
Mira Chen: yes, publish the incident as "Partial APAC capacity degradation; traffic steering in progress". Katie can post status with current mitigation list.
Katie L: posted status: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2201234567 (internal note linked).
Samir R: after 12m, canary move to apac2 reduced overall 5xx to 2.1% and tail latency back under 600ms. But apac2 token cost higher; need to watch billing and capacity.
Alex W: metrics look good. Recommend escalate to 80% over next 6m if stable.
Juan P: stepping to 80% now: `./routingctl --region apac --from apac1 --to apac2 --pct 80 --job rb-2201-canary-42 --continue`
Juan P: job complete. apac2 serving ~78% new sessions. apac1 still accepting sticky sessions.
Mira Chen: good. Now reduce brownout severity: keep reranker disabled for now, re-enable if we see sustained stability for 30m.
Alex W: also add temporary rate cap for free-tier API keys: `rlctl set --tier free --region apac --qps 3` to avoid thrash.
Katie L: free-tier cap applied. I DM’d account execs for large customers potentially affected.
Alex W: customer impact: small subset of heavy free-tier and some small SaaS customers may see increased errors or slower responses; enterprise SLA customers routed to dedicated pools — minimal impact.
Mira Chen: can we confirm no data loss and all requests either served or returned 429/503?
Samir R: logs show graceful rejections with 503 and 429 after quota change — no silent failures.
Mira Chen: great. Handing over to followup SRE team for monitoring. Next: postmortem owners and timeline. Who owns postmortem?
Juan P: I’ll own the postmortem — root cause likely provider hardware flakiness + insufficient automatic fallback.
Katie L: ops notes: costs elevated due to apac2 use, will file cost incident.
Alex W: runbook update task: add auto-detect and faster ramp for provider failover and an automated feature-brownout policy.
Mira Chen: agreed. Closing timeline: mitigation applied and traffic stabilized by last_message_ts. Will remain in watch for 60m and then start RCA. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: Incident rb-2201 recorded. Severity P1 -> mitigated; watch state initiated. Tags: apac, provider-fallback, brownout, quota-change.
